title: Beyond Aggregate WER: In-domain Adaptation, Learner Speech, Code-Switching, and Speaker Attribution in Online Spanish Learning Classrooms
abstract: arXiv:2610.38016v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) increasingly supplies transcripts for educational NLP, but aggregate word error rate (WER) can conceal errors concentrated in learner speech, multilingual turns, and speaker attribution. We compare platform-integrated, open-weight, adapted, and commercial ASR configurations on held-out sessions of online L2 Spanish interaction between L1 English learners and their instructors and tutors. Because English is the learner's shared first language, the interactions contain Spanish-only, English-only, and code-switched turns. Evaluation combines overall WER and character error rate (CER), WER disaggregated by speaker role and language context, and diarization error rate (DER). We also adapt Whisper large-v3 and MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize with LoRA using human-corrected in-domain classroom data. translated_title: 超越整体WER：在线西班牙语学习课堂中的领域内适配、学习者语音、语码转换与说话人归属
translated_abstract: 自动语音识别（ASR）日益为教育自然语言处理提供转录文本，但整体词错误率（WER）可能掩盖集中于学习者语音、多语轮次和说话人归属中的错误。我们在在线二语西班牙语互动的留出会话上，比较了平台集成、开源权重、适配后和商业等ASR配置，这些互动发生在母语为英语的学习者与其教师和辅导教师之间。由于英语是学习者的共同第一语言，这些互动包含纯西班牙语、纯英语和语码转换的轮次。评估结合了整体WER和字符错误率（CER）、按说话人角色和语言语境细分的WER，以及说话人分离错误率（DER）。我们还使用人工校对的领域内课堂数据，通过LoRA对Whisper large-v3和MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize进行了适配。MOSS适配在所有说话人角色和语言语境上带来了一致的改进，而Whisper则表现出……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究超越整体WER的评估方式，按说话人角色和语言语境细分错误来评估在线西班牙语课堂中的多种ASR系统，并通过LoRA领域内适配发现MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize在各维度上均带来一致改进。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates ASR in online Spanish classrooms beyond aggregate WER by disaggregating errors across speaker roles and language contexts, showing that LoRA in-domain adaptation of MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize yields consistent improvements across all dimensions.
